public_rationale: The 89% figure has corroboration as a statement about a particular annualised startup tally. That tally does not establish the $20 billion ceiling for the rest of the industry. Microsoft's disclosure is material contrary context under a broader reading, but its scope is not interchangeable with the startup sample. The combined claim remains unresolved; calling it contradicted would depend on choosing a company universe the speaker did not clearly supply.
limitations: The tally is available here through secondary reporting.
Partial corroboration of one component does not support the entire compound claim.
No realised annual-revenue requirement has been imposed.

public_payload.normalized_proposition: OpenAI and Anthropic represent 89% of the largest AI companies' revenues; excluding them, the AI industry makes at most $20B a year.

statement.excerpt: They want you to assume that all this money can’t be wrong, even though when you remove OpenAI and Anthropic (who represent 89% of the revenues of the largest AI companies) the AI industry is, at best, pulling in $20 billion in annual revenue.

from_speaker: 89% of the revenues of the largest AI companies
when you remove OpenAI and Anthropic
our_interpretation: The linked 89% figure refers to a tally of 34 leading private AI startups. Assess that percentage on the tally's annualised basis, not as realised revenue for an invented fiscal year.
The latest cited snapshot is from May 2026 and is used in a July 7 present-tense claim. The target interval covers that referenced snapshot through the post date.

The ordinary contextual reading of the $20 billion ceiling concerns the remaining generative-AI businesses. Whether that includes public-company AI businesses and infrastructure providers is materially ambiguous.
Do not assume that a sample of leading startups measures the entire remaining industry.
Excluding two companies defines the population; it is not a conditional forecast.
criteria.support_condition: The referenced tally establishes approximately 89% on its own annualised basis, and adequately comprehensive revenue evidence establishes no more than $20 billion for the remaining industry on a consistent basis.
criteria.contradiction_condition: A comparable reconstruction disproves the 89% tally, or comparable revenues for the relevant remaining industry exceed $20 billion. A broader or narrower company universe cannot be substituted without identifying the interpretation.

evidence.explanation: The report corroborates the 89% figure for a selected annualised startup tally. It expressly excludes public companies and AI cloud startups, so it does not establish the separate industry-wide ceiling.

evidence.excerpt: Our AI business surpassed $37 billion ARR
evidence.explanation: Microsoft's disclosure challenges a broad ceiling that includes public-company AI businesses. Its company-defined scope and possible revenue from the excluded labs prevent treating it as a clean contradiction of the startup-focused reading.

public_payload.what_would_resolve: The original tally and a sufficiently comprehensive revenue inventory for the remaining industry, with explicit coverage, snapshot dates and consistent annualisation and reseller treatment.
